LESSON: ATHLETICS AND MOSAIC

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.3: Athletics and Mosaic

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Athletics and Mosaic. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How has long distance running benefitted Kenya?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the phases in Triple jump
2. perform Triple jump for skill acquisition
3. identify long distance races in athletics
4. perform techniques for long distance running
5. create a mosaic pictorial composition inspired by an athletic event, g) acknowledge own and others’ efforts in performing Triple jump, skills in long

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ATHLETICS AND MOSAIC
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Athletics and Mosaic helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ATHLETICS AND MOSAIC
Study Athletics and Mosaic like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the phases in Triple jump

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the phases in Triple jump. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the phases in Triple jump.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Athletics and Mosaic” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the phases in Triple jump. Write or say your answer clearly.

3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Athletics and Mosaic in your own words.

Your turn

PART 5: Create a mosaic pictorial composition inspired by an athletic event, g) acknowledge own and others’ efforts in performing Triple jump, skills in long

What this means
In this part you learn to create a mosaic pictorial composition inspired by an athletic event, g) acknowledge own and others’ efforts in performing Triple jump, skills in long. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a mosaic pictorial composition inspired by an athletic event, g) acknowledge own and others’ efforts in performing Triple jump, skills in long.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Athletics and Mosaic in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a mosaic pictorial composition inspired by an athletic event, g) acknowledge own and others’ efforts in performing Triple jump, skills in long. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Athletics and Mosaic is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Athletics and Mosaic” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the phases in Triple jump)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Athletics and Mosaic in your own words. (skill: perform Triple jump for skill acquisition)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: identify long distance races in athletics)

Example 4: Show how “Athletics and Mosaic” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform techniques for long distance running)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Athletics and Mosaic to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the phases in Triple jump.
3. Practise this skill: perform Triple jump for skill acquisition.
4. Practise this skill: identify long distance races in athletics.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Athletics and Mosaic from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Athletics and Mosaic: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Athletics and Mosaic?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How has long distance running benefitted Kenya?
2. Why is it important to follow the phases of jumping in triple jump?
3. How can mosaic pictorial composition be used to improve the environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Athletics and Mosaic means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the phases in Triple jump.
5. Be able to: perform Triple jump for skill acquisition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
